name: Vertex-Deleted Three-Cube
definition: The subgraph of $Q_3$ induced by $\{0,1\}^3\setminus\{111\}$; every choice of the deleted cube vertex is isomorphic to this one.
properties: It is a partial cube, a daisy cube, an ample and maximum class of VC dimension two, a spread ample class, and a convex-geometry ideal, but it is not a hypercube or median: the coordinatewise majority of $110,101,011$ is the missing vertex $111$. Its three maximal facet cubes are the squares supported by the three coordinate pairs, and its corners are $110,101,011$, the neighbours of the missing vertex. More generally, the corners of $Q_n\setminus\{x\}$ are exactly the neighbours of $x$. Every proper pc-minor is median. Deleting any displayed coordinate by projection gives the full square $Q_2$, and conditioning on the side opposite the missing vertex also gives $Q_2$; neither is a vertex-deleted cube $Q_n^-$ with $n\ge2$.
